words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God intervenes between a believer and disbelief, and between a disbeliever and faith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يحول بين المؤمن وبين الكفر، وبين الكافر وبين الإيمان

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hakim graded Ibn Abbas’s stopped report sound and said the two compilers did not include it; Ibn Mardawayh’s raised version is weak, so the stopped version is sounder.
rows.anchor: رواه الحاكم في مستدركه موقوفا، وقال: صحيح ولم يخرجاه

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: مجاهد، وسعيد، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، وعطية، ومقاتل بن حيان، والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid, Sa'id, Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Suddi give Ibn Abbas’s explanation as well.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال مجاهد، وسعيد، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، وعطية، ومقاتل بن حيان، والسدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another report, Mujahid says God may intervene between a person and their heart until the person can no longer reason.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن مجاهد في قوله: {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} حتى تركه لا يعقل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says a person can neither believe nor disbelieve unless God permits it.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: يحول بين الإنسان وقلبه، فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن ولا يكفر إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah compares this statement with God being nearer to a person than the jugular vein.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة هو كقوله: {ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد}

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Prophetic reports accord with this verse’s warning about hearts being turned.
rows.anchor: وقد وردت الأحاديث عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بما يناسب هذه الآية

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet often prayed for the Turner of hearts to keep his heart firm in religion; he said hearts are between God’s fingers and He turns them as He wills.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول: " يا مقلب القلوب، ثبت قلبي على دينك"

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the Anas report hasan; some transmitters give a route through Jabir, but Ibn Kathir judges the Anas route more sound.
rows.anchor: وحديث أبي سفيان عن أنس أصح

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: بلال
rows.claim: Bilal reports that the Prophet prayed for the Turner of hearts to keep his heart firm in religion.
rows.anchor: عن بلال، رضي الله عنه، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو: "يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبي على دينك"

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Bilal’s report good in its chain, though interrupted; he says it meets the Sunan compilers’ standard, although they did not include it.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث جيد الإسناد إلا أن فيه انقطاعا

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: النواس بن سمعان
rows.claim: Al-Nawwas reports that every heart is between the fingers of the Merciful, who establishes or deviates it as He wills; the Prophet prayed for firm hearts and said the Scale is in the Merciful’s hand, lowered or raised.
rows.anchor: النواس بن سمعان الكلابي، رضي الله عنه، يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " ما من قلب إلا وهو

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet’s frequent prayer for a firm heart; he explained that God may lead a human heart astray or establish it.
rows.anchor: أن عائشة قالت: دعوات كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو بها: "يا مقلب القلوب

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salamah reports the Prophet’s prayer for firm hearts, his explanation that every human heart is between God’s fingers, and his teaching her a personal prayer for forgiveness, relief from anger, and protection from trials.
rows.anchor: سمعت أم سلمة تحدث: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكثر في دعائه يقول: "اللهم يا مقلب القلوب

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr reports that the hearts of Adam’s children are like one heart between the Merciful’s fingers, turned as He wills; the Prophet prayed for them to be turned to obedience.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو؛ أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إن قلوب بني آدم بين إصبعين

words: واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Muslim alone, alongside al-Nasa'i, included Abdullah ibn Amr’s report through Haywah ibn Shurayh; al-Bukhari did not include it.
rows.anchor: انفرد بإخراجه مسلم عن البخاري، فرواه مع النسائي من حديث حيوة بن شريح المصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims camped on the nearer side of the valley toward Medina, while the polytheists camped on the farther side toward Mecca.
rows.anchor: أي: إذ أنتم نزول بعدوة الوادي الدنيا القريبة إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan below the Muslims was Abu Sufyan’s trade caravan, positioned toward the seashore.
rows.anchor: العير الذي فيه أبو سفيان بما معه من التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the two sides arranged a meeting, they would have missed it because the circumstances made the encounter unlikely.
rows.anchor: {ولو تواعدتم} أي: أنتم والمشركون إلى مكان

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr that, if the meeting had been planned, the Muslims would have turned away on learning the enemy’s numbers and their own smaller force.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: وحدثني يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير، عن أبيه في هذه الآية

words: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought about what He willed through His power: strengthening Islam and its people and humbling polytheism and its people, without the Muslims arranging it, by His subtle providence.
rows.anchor: ليقضي الله ما أراد بقدرته من إعزاز الإسلام وأهله، وإذلال الشرك وأهله

words: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا
rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik says the Prophet and Muslims set out seeking Quraysh’s caravan, but God brought them face to face with their enemy without an appointment.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث كعب بن مالك قال: إنما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمون يريدون عير قريش

rows.speaker: عمير بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Umayr ibn Ishaq reports that Abu Sufyan’s Syrian caravan and Abu Jahl’s force to protect it reached Badr unaware of one another, until water carriers met and the troops advanced.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عون، عن عمير بن إسحاق قال: أقبل أبو سفيان في الركب من الشام، وخرج أبو جهل ليمنعه

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts how scouts Basbas and Adi learned the caravan’s arrival; Abu Sufyan found Yathrib date pits in their camels’ droppings, hurried the caravan along the coast, and told Quraysh to return.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق في السيرة: ومضى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على وجهه

words: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا
rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports Abu Jahl refusing to return after the caravan was saved, insisting Quraysh camp at Badr for three days of feasting and display so Arabs would fear them.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو جهل: والله (4) لا نرجع حتى نأتي بدرا

words: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا
rows.speaker: الأخنس بن شريق
rows.claim: Al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq persuaded Banu Zuhrah that God had saved their property and leader, so they returned; Banu Adi also did not attend Badr.
rows.anchor: فقال الأخنس بن شريق: يا معشر بني زهرة، إن الله قد نجى أموالكم، ونجى صاحبكم، فارجعوا

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that the Prophet’s scouts captured Quraysh water carriers; after the Prophet rebuked the companions for beating truthful witnesses and releasing liars, he learned the enemy numbered about 900–1,000 and heard its leading names.
rows.anchor: إذا صدقاكم ضربتموهما، وإذا كذباكم تركتموهما. صدقا، والله إنهما لقريش

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: After hearing the captives’ account of Quraysh’s prominent leaders, the Prophet told the Muslims that Mecca had cast its choicest people before them.
rows.anchor: فأقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الناس فقال: "هذه مكة قد ألقت إليكم أفلاذ كبدها"

words: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا
rows.speaker: سعد بن معاذ
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh proposed a shelter and mounts for the Prophet at Badr, with a route to join their supporters if defeated; he said absent Muslims loved and would support the Prophet had they known of the battle. The Prophet praised and prayed for him, and the shelter was built for the Prophet and Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: أن سعد بن معاذ قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، لما التقى الناس يوم بدر: يا رسول الله، ألا نبني لك عريشا

words: ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا
rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: As Quraysh approached Badr at dawn, the Prophet prayed for their defeat, describing them as boastful, arrogant, and opposing God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: قال: "اللهم هذه (6) قريش قد أقبلت بفخرها

words: ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيا من حي عن بينة
rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains that the event lets disbelief persist after proof and signs, and lets belief arise on their evidence.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: أي ليكفر من كفر بعد الحجة، لما رأى من الآية والعبرة

words: ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيا من حي عن بينة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir endorses Ibn Ishaq’s explanation: God joined the forces unexpectedly to make truth prevail and its proof decisive, leaving no excuse; the disbeliever persists knowingly in falsehood, while the believer accepts guidance with insight. Faith gives hearts life.
rows.anchor: وهذا تفسير جيد. وبسط ذلك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites Aisha’s account of the slander episode: “those who perished” refers to those who spoke falsehood, slander, and calumny about her.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة في قصة الإفك: في هلك من هلك أي: قال فيها ما قال من الكذب والبهتان والإفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the Muslims’ prayers, supplications, and cries for help, and knows that they deserve victory over their stubborn, hostile disbelieving enemies.
rows.anchor: أي: لدعائكم وتضرعكم واستغاثتكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing hypocrites who stayed from campaigns through aversion, denial, and doubt, the passage turns to sinners who stayed from laziness and comfort despite believing the truth.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى حال المنافقين المتخلفين عن الغزاة رغبة عنها وتكذيبا وشكا

words: اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admitted their sins to God and mixed good deeds with bad; they remain under God’s pardon and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أقروا بها واعترفوا فيما بينهم وبين ربهم، ولهم أعمال أخر صالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse was revealed about particular people, Ibn Kathir says its scope includes all sincere, erring sinners who are tainted by wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية -وإن كانت نزلت في أناس معينين -إلا أنها عامة في كل المذنبين الخاطئين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about Abu Lubabah, who signaled to Banu Qurayzah that the outcome for them was slaughter.
rows.anchor: في أبي لبابة لما قال لبني قريظة: إنه الذبح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerned Abu Lubabah and companions who stayed behind from Tabuk; accounts differ whether five, seven, or nine joined him. They bound themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet released and pardoned them after revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: {وآخرون} نزلت في أبي لبابة وجماعة من أصحابه

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: In a dream report narrated by Samurah ibn Jundub, the Prophet sees a mixed-appearance group transformed after bathing in a river; angels identify them as people who mixed good and evil deeds, whom God forgave. Al-Bukhari gives it in abbreviated form here.
rows.anchor: حدثنا سمرة بن جندب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا: "أتاني الليلة آتيان

words: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The events affirm God’s promise to help His messengers and believers in this life and on the Day of Witnesses, and His promise to replace unjust peoples with those who fear Him.
rows.anchor: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا ويوم يقوم الأشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering day includes the first and last of humanity, with no one left behind, as stated in 18:47.
rows.anchor: أي: أولهم وآخرهم، فلا يبقى منهم أحد، كما قال: {وحشرناهم فلم نغادر منهم أحدا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is a tremendous day attended by all angels and messengers and gathering all creatures—humans, jinn, birds, wild animals, and livestock—for the perfectly just Judge, who wrongs none and multiplies good deeds.
rows.anchor: يوم عظيم تحضره الملائكة كلهم، ويجتمع فيه الرسل جميعهم، وتحشر فيه الخلائق بأسرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Resurrection is delayed until the appointed, finite term expires and all the people of Adam’s descendants whose existence God decreed have appeared; the term cannot be extended or shortened.
rows.anchor: قد سبقت كلمة الله وقضاؤه وقدره، في وجود أناس معدودين من ذرية آدم، وضرب مدة معينة

words: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one speaks that day except by God’s permission, as also stated in 78:38 and 20:108.
rows.anchor: إلا بإذن الله تعالى، كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In the lengthy intercession report in the two Sahih collections, only messengers speak on that day, praying, ‘O God, grant safety.’
rows.anchor: في حديث الشفاعة الطويل: "ولا يتكلم يومئذ إلا الرسل، ودعوى الرسل يومئذ: اللهم سلم سلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among those gathered are the wretched and the fortunate, corresponding to the groups in Paradise and the Blaze in 42:7.
rows.anchor: أي: فمن أهل الجمع شقي ومنهم سعيد، كما قال: {فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير}

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar asked whether deeds concern a settled decree or an unfinished matter. The Prophet said the decree and pens had settled it, yet each person is made easy for what they were created to do.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر، عن عمر (9) رضي الله عنه، قال: لما نزلت {فمنهم شقي وسعيد} سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the zafir is in the throat and the shahiq in the chest: their exhalation and inhalation reflect their torment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر أي: تنفسهم زفير

words: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن جرير
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says Arabs use ‘as long as the heavens and earth endure’ and similar phrases about night and day to mean forever.
rows.anchor: من عادة العرب إذا أرادت أن تصف الشيء بالدوام أبدا قالت:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir also allows that the phrase refers to the afterlife’s own heavens and earth, since these will exist there, citing their transformation in 14:48.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن المراد بما دامت السموات والأرض: الجنس؛ لأنه لا بد في عالم الآخرة من سموات وأرض

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says the reference is to a different heaven and earth replacing these, and permanence lasts while those endure.
rows.anchor: قال: تبدل سماء غير (4) هذه السماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says, in a report transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim from Mujahid through Sufyan ibn Husayn and al-Hakam, that each Garden has its own heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: ذكر عن سفيان بن حسين، عن الحكم، عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس قوله: {ما دامت السماوات والأرض}

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam interprets the phrase as lasting as long as earth remains earth and heaven remains heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: ما دامت الأرض أرضا، والسماء سماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is also found in 6:128. Al-Tabari, as reported by Ibn Kathir, prefers the interpretation that it concerns monotheist sinners released from Hell through intercession and then God’s mercy; only those destined for eternal punishment remain.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى: {النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله إن ربك حكيم عليم}

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن جرير
rows.claim: Al-Tabari’s preferred view makes the exception apply to sinful monotheists: intercession frees major sinners, then the Most Merciful removes from Hell anyone who ever professed that there is no god but God, even if they did no other good.
rows.anchor: أن الاستثناء عائد على العصاة من أهل التوحيد، ممن يخرجهم الله من النار بشفاعة الشافعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says many early and later scholars accept this view, citing reports from Companions Umar, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, Abdullah ibn Amr, Jabir, Abu Sa'id, and Successors Abu Mijlaz and al-Sha'bi.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي عليه كثير من العلماء قديما وحديثا في تفسير هذه الآية الكريمة

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir mentions an unusual report from Abu Umamah in al-Tabarani’s al-Mu'jam al-Kabir but says its chain is weak.
rows.anchor: وورد حديث غريب في معجم الطبراني الكبير، عن أبي أمامة صدى بن عجلان الباهلي، ولكن سنده ضعيف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says God knows best what His exception means.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الله أعلم بثنياه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the exception is abrogated by the statement that they will remain therein forever in 4:57.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: هي منسوخة بقوله: {خالدين فيها أبدا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fortunate are the followers of the messengers, and Paradise is their home.
rows.anchor: {وأما الذين سعدوا} وهم أتباع الرسل

words: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise remain there forever; the exception means their continuing bliss is dependent on God’s will and gracious favor, not something independently obligatory upon Him. He inspires their praise as naturally as breathing.
rows.anchor: معنى الاستثناء هاهنا: أن دوامهم فيما هم فيه من النعيم، ليس أمرا واجبا بذاته

rows.speaker: الضحاك، والحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan al-Basri say the exception concerns monotheist sinners who had been in Hell and were then brought out.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك، والحسن البصري: هي في حق عصاة الموحدين الذين كانوا في النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, and others gloss the gift as uncut or unending; this closes off any inference of cessation after the mention of God’s will.
rows.anchor: {عطاء غير مجذوذ} أي: غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir contrasts punishment, subject to God’s will and grounded in His justice and wisdom, with the reassurance of an unbroken gift; he links the passage to 11:107 and 21:23.
rows.anchor: كما قال {لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون} [الأنبياء:23]

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted declaring that Paradise’s people and Hell’s people have everlasting residence without death; a report in both Sahih collections adds that the people of Paradise never die, age, fall ill, or suffer.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين (4) أيضا: "فيقال (5) يا أهل الجنة، إن لكم أن تعيشوا فلا تموتوا أبدا
